stops.name: Iglesia de la Merced, la Virgen Generala
stops.campa: In the thanksgiving procession the image of Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes is borne through streets still smelling of powder. Before the whole army Belgrano approaches the litter and places his general's baton in the Virgin's carved hands, naming her Generala of the Army of the North. The soldiers roar; the victory has been assigned to its true commander. From this day the army marches under a patroness with rank, and the baton stays in Tucumán, in her keeping, forever.

stops.name: Río Pasaje, el Juramento
stops.campa: Marching north to finish Tristán, the army halts at the ford of the Río Pasaje on 13 February 1813. Word has come that the Asamblea del Año XIII now holds sovereignty. Belgrano forms the army on the bank, raises the white-and-blue flag, brought out of its ordered hiding at last, and swears obedience to the Assembly; rank by rank the army swears after him, arms presented over the brown water. The river takes a new name from that hour: Juramento. Even the map remembers the oath.

stops.name: Campo Castañares, la Batalla de Salta
stops.campa: Guided through the hills by Captain Apolinario Saravia along a path the enemy holds impossible, the army falls on Salta from the north, where no attack can come. On 20 February 1813, through rain and over the Campo Castañares, the flag of Rosario goes into fire for the first time in a pitched battle, and wins entire. Tristán's army is not defeated; it is captured whole, three thousand men grounding arms in the plaza. Nothing like it has been seen in the war: a royal army erased in an afternoon, under colors ten months old.

stops.name: Salta, el perdón de Tristán y la fosa común
stops.campa: The victor's terms scandalize his own government: the entire royalist army is freed on its oath never again to bear arms against the patria; Tristán, his defeated friend from student days in Spain, is embraced, not imprisoned. The dead of both sides go into one grave beneath one cross bearing the legend the tradition guards: victors and vanquished. Buenos Aires rages at his clemency; Belgrano answers that his word is given and will be kept. The canon keeps the pardon among his victories: the harder, higher kind.

stops.name: Jujuy, los cuarenta mil pesos y las cuatro escuelas
stops.campa: The Assembly votes the hero of Tucumán and Salta forty thousand pesos, a fortune, in reward. Belgrano, poor and in debt, refuses it for himself in a single sentence and endows with it four public primary schools, Tarija, Jujuy, Tucumán, Santiago del Estero, writing with his own hand the regulations: the master's duties, the poor children's rights, the love of order and of the patria to be taught. Two centuries on, the debt of the schools remains the most famous unpaid account in the nation's ledger.
stops.quote: He creído propio de mi honor y de los deseos que me inflaman por la prosperidad de mi patria, destinar los expresados cuarenta mil pesos para la dotación de cuatro escuelas públicas de primeras letras.
stops.quote_source: Oficio de Belgrano a la Asamblea del Año XIII, 31 de marzo de 1813

stops.name: Potosí, el cuartel general en la Villa Imperial
stops.campa: The vanguard under Díaz Vélez enters Potosí on 7 May; by midwinter Belgrano himself establishes his headquarters in the Villa Imperial under the red cone of the Cerro Rico, the mountain that ate a world. He governs gently where Castelli governed hot: mass in the cathedral, honors to the cabildo, proclamations in Quechua to the pueblos originarios, whom he calls brothers and dreams of restoring. The silver city watches the courteous general and half believes. North, at Pezuela's camp, a real army is being drilled at leisure.

stops.name: Pampa de Vilcapugio, la batalla perdida al ganarse
stops.campa: On the bare altiplano pampa of Vilcapugio, ringed by granite peaks, the armies meet on 1 October 1813. The patriot right sweeps everything before it; victory is in Belgrano's hand, and then a dead man's trumpet, a royalist call sounded on the wrong field, wheels the winning wing away in the dust, and Pezuela's reformed line takes the day. Belgrano stands with the flag on the pampa gathering the fugitives around him, and by nightfall has saved a remnant and the colors. At Macha he begins again, as he always begins again.

stops.name: Ayohúma, la dignidad en la derrota
stops.campa: Forty days later, on the plain of Ayohúma, 'head of the dead' in the old tongue, the rebuilt army fights its last. Pezuela's guns dominate from the heights; the patriot line is broken and broken again. Through the wreck moves María Remedios del Valle, the Black captain the soldiers call Madre de la Patria, carrying water and cartridges under fire; the niñas de Ayohúma bind wounds at the field's edge. Belgrano brings four hundred men off the plain and leaves his battle-flags hidden at the chapel of Titiri, near Macha, where a century later they are found: the oldest flags of the nation, sleeping in the defeat.

stops.name: Potosí, la mina bajo la Casa de Moneda
stops.campa: Evacuating Potosí with Pezuela at his heels, Belgrano orders the Casa de Moneda, the empire's silver heart, mined with powder, to deny it to the enemy. The fuse is lit as the rearguard rides out. It does not fire: the tradition tells that a hand, Potosino or providential, cut the slow-match in the dark, and the great mint stands to this day. The canon lets both readings stand: the general hard enough to order it, and the mercy that unmade the order.

stops.name: Jujuy, la retirada y la espera de San Martín
stops.campa: The army drips south down the quebradas, sick, shoeless, unpaid, screened by Güemes' gauchos who close the passes behind it like doors. Belgrano, fevered and coughing blood, holds the wreck together by presence alone, and writes south to the colonel of the Granaderos who is riding up to relieve him. There is no jealousy in the letter: only the plain relief of a man who has carried the north for two years and sees help on the road at Christmas.
stops.quote: Mi corazón toma nuevo aliento cada instante que pienso que usted se me acerca, porque estoy firmemente persuadido de que con usted se salvará la patria.
stops.quote_source: Carta de Belgrano a José de San Martín, diciembre de 1813

stops.name: Posta de Yatasto, la entrega del ejército a San Martín
stops.campa: At the posta of Yatasto, so the canon fixes it, on 30 January 1814, the two liberators meet: Belgrano defeated, ill and serene; San Martín with the future in his saddlebags. The elder hands over the Army of the North and asks to serve under his replacement as a simple officer of the man sent to replace him. In the posta's gallery the two talk long of the war, of monarchy and of America; San Martín will say ever after that Belgrano is the best we have in the south. The relay of the revolution passes hands here, without a shadow between the runners.
stops.quote: Ayudaré a usted con mis conocimientos del país; serviré con el mayor gusto a las órdenes de usted.
stops.quote_source: Belgrano to San Martín on the handover of command, January 1814, as kept by the tradition (cf. their correspondence)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, embarque de la misión a Europa
stops.campa: Summoned south, tried again and again vindicated, the general is given a new weapon: diplomacy. On 28 December 1814 Belgrano and Bernardino Rivadavia sail from Buenos Aires for Europe, instructed to seek from Spain or from any decent throne the recognition of these provinces: independence if possible, a constitutional prince if necessary. Ferdinand is restored, Napoleon falling, the whole world turning back to kings; the revolution sends its most honest man to negotiate with the tide.
